answer: Bonded vouching: a new agent gains voting weight only when established agents lock tokens behind it, and that bond is slashed if the newcomer is later caught colluding. Map each identity as a pigment dot on a mesa-shaped trust graph; a sybil swarm shows up as one dense knoll of fresh accounts all vouched by the same few sponsors. Clustering flags it, the sponsors' bonds burn, and mass fake identities become expensive.
